# Passenger Rail Corridor Proposal: Albany, NY to New York City, NY

> **Illustrative estimates: costs, schedules and funding figures in this draft come from an uncalibrated planning model and approximate program parameters. They are not budgets or engineering estimates.**

## Executive Summary

This proposal evaluates three passenger rail alternatives for the Albany, NY to New York City, NY corridor, based on 5000 simulation runs per alternative. Alternative 1, the Existing corridor upgrade, achieves the highest composite score of 87.3 out of 100, while also offering the lowest median cost, shortest median schedule, and serving the most population. The New direct alignment (Alternative 2) provides the shortest length at 140 miles, while Alternative 3 (Maximum population served) extends to 160 miles. All three alternatives connect 3 stations: New York City, Albany, and Poughkeepsie.

## Corridor Description

The corridor spans from Albany, NY to New York City, NY. Alternative 1 (Existing corridor upgrade) covers 145 miles with 98.7% share on existing rail, serving 12.21 million people within a 10 miles population buffer. It incorporates 3 stations (New York City, Albany, and Poughkeepsie), 13 river crossings, and 6 environmental flag entries. Alternative 2 (New direct alignment) spans 140 miles with 24.4% share on existing rail, serving 12.17 million people, with 1 river crossing and 1 environmental flag entry. Alternative 3 (Maximum population served) covers 160 miles with 48.2% share on existing rail, serving 12.12 million people, with 2 river crossings and 2 environmental flag entries.

## Cost and Schedule Range

Costs discussed are illustrative estimates, not budgets. Alternative 1 has a median (P50) capital cost of $6.1B, with a P10 low of $5.0B and a P90 high of $7.6B. Its median (P50) time to opening is 11.0 years, ranging from a P10 of 9.5 years to a P90 of 12.6 years. Alternative 2 requires a median (P50) capital cost of $9.2B (P10 of $7.8B, P90 of $10.9B) and a median (P50) schedule of 12.8 years (P10 of 11.3 years, P90 of 14.5 years). Alternative 3 has a median (P50) capital cost of $9.2B (P10 of $7.7B, P90 of $10.9B) and a median (P50) schedule of 12.4 years (P10 of 10.9 years, P90 of 14.0 years).

## Funding Strategy

The funding strategy combines federal grant programs and financing tools. Key grant sources include the Corridor Identification and Development Program (Corridor ID) with a federal amount of $500K for planning, and the Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (National) with a federal amount of $3.0B, representing a federal share of median cost of 48.8% for Alternative 1, 32.4% for Alternative 2, and 32.6% for Alternative 3. Additional grants include Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements (CRISI) with $250M (4.1% federal share of median cost for Alternative 1, and 2.7% for Alternatives 2 and 3) and BUILD Grants with $25M (0.4% federal share of median cost for Alternative 1, and 0.3% for Alternatives 2 and 3). Alternative 1 also identifies $246M under Federal-State Partnership (Northeast Corridor), representing a 4.0% federal share of median cost. Non-federal match financing can utilize Railroad Rehabilitation and Improvement Financing (RRIF) loans, with estimated loan amounts of $1.2B for Alternative 1, and $1.8B for Alternatives 2 and 3. Capital costs are illustrative estimates, not budgets.

## Risks

Key project risks across the alternatives include physical, environmental, and financial constraints. Alternative 1 features 13 river crossings and 6 environmental flag entries due to its alignment footprint. Alternative 2 involves 1 river crossing and 1 environmental flag entry, but requires extensive greenfield acquisition with only 24.4% share on existing rail. Alternative 3 includes 2 river crossings and 2 environmental flag entries across 160 miles. All cost figures represent illustrative estimates, not budgets, and schedules remain subject to P90 high risks reaching 12.6 years for Alternative 1, 14.5 years for Alternative 2, and 14.0 years for Alternative 3.

## Next Steps

Recommended next steps for corridor advancement: * Secure $500K in planning funds under the Corridor Identification and Development Program for Step 1 scoping. * Initiate preliminary engineering and environmental studies to review the environmental flag entries and river crossings across candidate routes. * Formulate a phased capital application strategy for the Federal-State Partnership for Intercity Passenger Rail (National) program to address median (P50) funding requirements.
